title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing, Pitch Decks, Case Studies, and Security FAQ
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference sales enablement artifacts for pre-sales and field motions focused on: positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch-deck templates, pricing guidance, customer case study assets, and a prospect-facing security FAQ.
- Intended audience: sales reps, solutions engineers, AE managers, customer success managers, and partner enablement leads.

How to use this document
1) Reference the Positioning & Messaging section when preparing outreach sequences and slide decks.
2) Use Competitive Briefs as the source of truth for objection handling.
3) Follow Pricing Guidance for first-pass pricing and contract levers; escalate non-standard requests to PricingOps.
4) Use the Pitch Deck checklist and templates for discovery and executive demos.
5) Pull Case Study assets for deal proof points.
6) Provide the Security FAQ to technical buyers; sensitive security artifacts live in Security & Compliance (link in Related Pages).

Owner and updates
- Playbook owner: Go-to-market Enablement (owner_team).
- Content owner: Aisha Kumar (author).
- Review cadence: quarterly or on major product/price changes. Reviewer group: Marco Alvarez (Head of Sales Eng), Leah Chen (Product Marketing), Priya Singh (Security PM).

Positioning & Messaging

Core narrative (elevator pitch)
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We shift competitive advantage from model ownership to serving—by making latency, cost, reliability, and deployment flexibility first-class.

Key value props (top-line bullets for sales outreach)
- Production-grade inference: predictable latency and throughput with SLA-backed Dedicated deployments.
- Unified runtime across environments: same API and tooling for Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: smart routing, model fallbacks, and multi-tier capacity to prevent customer-facing outages.
- Observability & ops: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and rollout tooling (canary/A-B/auto-fallback).

Messaging by persona
- Developer / Engineering: emphasize SDKs, fast onboarding, model catalog, streaming, and tool-calling. Include example snippet: curl + SDK quickstart (link to Quickstarts).
- ML/Platform Engineer: emphasize model lifecycle for serving, version pinning, rollout controls, quantization profiles, and perf/benchmark reports.
- Security/InfoSec: highlight private deployment options, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and SOC/ISO compliance artifacts.
- Product / Biz: focus on unit economics and observability (per-route cost), predictable capacity for launches, and model-quality guardrails.

Proof points and metrics
- Latency SLOs: typical 99th percentile generation latency for 1k-token requests on Dedicated = 120–220 ms per token depending on model family and hw profile (see Runtime Perf Summary).
- Cost savings: customers report 20–60% unit cost reduction after enabling caching/batching and quantization recommendations (typical range by workload).
- Availability: Dedicated deployments SLA 99.9% monthly; Hosted API runbook and region fallbacks maintained by SRE.

Competitive Briefs (Top competitors and rebuttals)

Format: For each competitor below, use the short summary, perceived strengths, typical customer asks, and suggested rebuttals/demo play.

Competitor: Cloud Managed Endpoint Vendors (Major public clouds)
- Strengths: deep cloud integration, enterprise procurement familiarity, global region footprint.
- Typical asks: "Can you match our cloud billing and identity integrations?"
- Rebuttal / Play: Emphasize Redwood's inference-optimized runtime, explicit per-route cost visibility, and optimized kernels that reduce total cost. Offer reference architecture and marketplace listing + procurement templates.

Competitor: LLM API Providers (simplicity-first, single-model stacks)
- Strengths: ease-of-use, single unified model offering, heavy marketing.
- Typical asks: "Why not use their API?"
- Rebuttal / Play: Redwood differentiates on deployment flexibility (Dedicated/Private), production observability, and unit-cost controls. Demonstrate cost/latency comparison on customer-like workload using Redwood demo harness.

Competitor: Self-hosted Inference Stacks / Open-source Runtimes
- Strengths: full control, potentially lower infra costs at scale.
- Typical asks: "Why not build our own?"
- Rebuttal / Play: Building and operating high-throughput inference is expensive and time-consuming. Use Redwood’s metrics: engineering time to production (weeks vs months), ongoing ops headcount, and fall-back features (rollouts, runtime optimizations). Offer a TCO worksheet.

Competitive win themes and battlecards
- Cost-sensitive, high-throughput customers: emphasize batching/caching profiles and quantization; show concrete token-cost reductions.
- Highly regulated customers: lead with Private deployment and KMS + audit logs; offer on-prem packaging reference architecture.
- Platform teams: emphasize consistent API and pinning/rollout controls to enforce ML lifecycle best practices.

Pitch Deck Guidance and Templates

Deck types and recommended slide order
1) Discovery / Intro Deck (10–12 slides)
   - Title & hook (customer-specific pain)
   - Problems: operational cost, latency unpredictability, model quality regressions
   - Redwood solution overview (one-liner + architecture diagram)
   - Key capabilities: API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize
   - Concrete proof points (latency/cost numbers, logos, badges)
   - Deployment options & timeline (POC -> Pilot -> Prod)
   - Next steps & ask (POC scope, success criteria, decision timeline)
2) Technical Deep Dive (20–30 slides)
   - Runtime architecture and kernel selection
   - Batching/caching and KV cache examples
   - Quantization profiles and expected perf impact by model family
   - Security & compliance details (KMS, audit, network isolation)
   - Operations & runbooks (auto-scaling, fallbacks)
3) Executive / Business Case (5–8 slides)
   - ROI & unit economics (TCO worksheet highlights)
   - Strategic fit and partnership model

Deck best practices
- Customize the problem statement and 2–3 proof points for the prospect.
- Include a slide with concrete POC success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput targets, cost per 1k tokens).
- Use customer logos/case studies with one-line outcomes (e.g., "Reduced inference unit cost by 37% after enablement").
- Always include 'Next steps' with owners and dates.

Pricing Guidance

Standard offers (first-pass guidance)
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + per-embedding unit). Provide standard SKU table: small / medium / large token bands with list price per 1k tokens (see Pricing Guidelines doc for current numeric tiers).
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): monthly committed vGPU pools with throughput guarantees and discounted unit pricing. Standard contract lengths: 12 / 36 months.
- Private (VPC / On-Prem): platform fee + deployment + support SLA tier; pricing modeled as upfront onboarding + monthly platform fee and optional managed services.

Discounting and commercial levers
- Allowed commercial levers (AE authorized): trial credits (up to $10k), first 3 months 50% off for 12-month Dedicated contracts.
- Escalation path: any >25% discount or changes to SLAs must be approved by PricingOps.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance packages, premium SLAs (separately priced).

POC commercial model (recommended)
1) Offer a 4–6 week POC with: limited Dedicated capacity or hosted usage credits, onboarding support (SSE/SE hours), and agreed success criteria.
2) POC acceptance criteria should be measurable: e.g., achieve 95% of target throughput at <X ms p99 latency, or cost per 1k tokens below target.
3) Transition plan: convert usage/commit to Dedicated contract or continue on Hosted at negotiated rates.

Legal and procurement notes
- Use standard SOW/MLA templates (link) and consult SalesOps for enterprise procurement requirements.
- For Private deployments, include scope for network setup, KMS key exchange, and SOC/ISO evidence package delivery windows.

Case Studies & Proof Assets

Structure for quick case pull (ready-made snippets for slides/email)
- Customer name (anonymize if required), vertical, problem statement, Redwood solution, measurable outcome, keys to success, SE/PM contacts.

Examples (anonymized)
- SaaS Analytics Platform (vertical: SaaS)
  - Problem: Spiky inference during daily reporting windows causing high cost and latency.
  - Solution: Dedicated GPU pools + intelligent batching and KV caching.
  - Outcome: 45% unit-cost reduction and p99 latency improvement from 400ms to 120ms on critical flows.

- Financial Services Regulated Customer (vertical: FinServ)
  - Problem: Need private inference with strict audit trails and on-prem data processing.
  - Solution: Private deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit log integration; on-prem packaging.
  - Outcome: Passed internal audit; reduced data access surface; deployment completed in 10 weeks.

Security FAQ for Prospects (Tech buyer primer)

Purpose: Provide concise answers to the most common security and compliance questions asked by prospects. For deeper artifacts (SOC reports, penetration tests) link to Security & Compliance.

Q: Where do you store our data and how is it isolated?
A: For Hosted customers, inference data is stored in region-specific encrypted object stores with strict access controls. Dedicated and Private customers can choose isolated tenancy and VPC-level network segmentation; Private deployments can be fully on-prem.

Q: How is customer data encrypted?
A: Data at rest and in transit is encrypted using AES-256/TLS 1.2+. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key control.

Q: Do you offer audit logs and monitoring for compliance?
A: Yes — audit logging includes request/response metadata, key events (deployment/rollout), and admin activity. Logs can be exported to customer SIEMs or stored in customer-controlled buckets.

Q: How do you handle multi-tenancy and data separation?
A: Dedicated and Private options provide strong tenant isolation: Dedicated via reserved GPU pools and network segmentation; Private via dedicated control plane and optional on-prem packaging. Hosted has strict logical separation and role-based access controls.

Q: What certifications and third-party attestations are available?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is working toward ISO 27001. We provide customer-specific evidence packages under NDA.

Q: How do you handle vulnerability management and pen testing?
A: We run regular vulnerability scans, quarterly internal pen tests, and annual third-party penetration tests. Critical CVEs follow our 30/90 remediation SLA depending on severity.

Q: What is your incident response posture?
A: We maintain an Incident Response runbook, SIRT team, and customer notification SLAs: initial notification within 4 hours for Sev1 incidents and post-incident reports within 7 business days.

Q: Can we run in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes — our on-prem packaging supports air-gapped deployments; planning typically requires 6–12 weeks depending on integration scope.

Operational play and sample rebuttals for security objections
- If asked about "data privacy during POC": propose isolated test tenancy + logging export and a short-term NDA.
- If asked about "keys and KMS": provide example KMS key exchange flow and work with Security PM (Priya Singh) to schedule architectural review.
